content:
Hello,

I'm trying to migrate the kernel DMA API from transmute.rs to zerocopy, which
@Alistair Popple asked about in June [1]. The bound is on Coherent<T> itself,
so every unsafe impl transmute::{AsBytes, FromBytes} on a type used with it has to
become a zerocopy derive at once. That works on my tree (+16/-19), and the remaining
users are all in nova.

The one I cannot solve is GspFwWprMeta, because it has two anonymous unions.
#[derive(IntoBytes)] on a union needs --cfg zerocopy_derive_union_into_bytes,
which the kernel does not pass, and the most_traits option @Alexandre Courbot
suggested in June [2] gives exactly the same error.

So I think his other option, updating the generator, is the place to fix it. The two
variants of each union are layout-identical and nova only ever writes one, so if the
generator wrote that variant directly instead of a union, the problem would be gone
for r570 and r000 both. The r000 bindings are being added now [3], so this looks like
a good time.

One question first, which I could not answer from the code: @Danilo Krummrich,
does the allocation path of Coherent<T> really need the AsBytes half? The two
SAFETY comments that mention T: AsBytes + FromBytes do not rely on the AsBytes
part, and I found no comment explaining it. If it is not needed there, none of the
above matters.

If I missed something, please let me know.
Best regards, SeungJong

[1] https://lore.kernel.org/all/20260628-dma-zerocopy-bridge-v1-0-9a2895ebe30d@gmail.com/
[2] https://lore.kernel.org/all/DJLCLH7GDSBW.28J4PZW0FD60B@nvidia.com/
[3] https://lore.kernel.org/all/20261103-r000_rebase_on_cmdq-rpc-v1-0-189f9ff3bfd2@nvidia.com/
Is there a reason we can't just pass --cfg zerocopy_derive_union_into_bytes?

@Josh Liebow-Feeser @Jack Wrenn

Is this part of the docs still accurate? i.e. how likely you think we can mess it up? I am asking since it seems to be from late 2024, so perhaps there are some good news? :)

/// # Unions
///
/// Currently, union bit validity is [up in the air][union-validity], and so
/// zerocopy does not support `#[derive(IntoBytes)]` on unions by default.
/// However, implementing `IntoBytes` on a union type is likely sound on all
/// existing Rust toolchains - it's just that it may become unsound in the
/// future. You can opt-in to `#[derive(IntoBytes)]` support on unions by
/// passing the unstable `zerocopy_derive_union_into_bytes` cfg:
///
/// ```shell
/// $ RUSTFLAGS='--cfg zerocopy_derive_union_into_bytes' cargo build
/// ```
///
/// However, it is your responsibility to ensure that this derive is sound on
/// the specific versions of the Rust toolchain you are using! We make no
/// stability or soundness guarantees regarding this cfg, and may remove it at
/// any point.
///
/// We are actively working with Rust to stabilize the necessary language
/// guarantees to support this in a forwards-compatible way, which will enable
/// us to remove the cfg gate. As part of this effort, we need to know how much
/// demand there is for this feature. If you would like to use `IntoBytes` on
/// unions, [please let us know][discussion].
///
/// [union-validity]: https://github.com/rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines/issues/438
/// [discussion]: https://github.com/google/zerocopy/discussions/1802

Thanks!
Let me move the topic to #zerocopy, by the way.
This topic was moved here from #General > zerocopy: how to handle unions in the generated bindings? by Miguel Ojeda.
It’s unfortunately still pretty up in the air: https://github.com/rust-lang/reference/pull/2340
The latest update is that Jack and I had a conversation after that PR got closed and we think we have a way of resolving the concerns raised there
